biological_interpretation: Loss of the PP2A A-alpha scaffold does not produce one uniform cholesterol response; the sterol module is induced in specific midbrain/hypothalamic contexts while the SREBP2/HMGCR arm is depressed in thalamic and cortical neurons.
caveats: The data are transcript-level and do not measure PP2A holoenzyme composition, phosphoproteins, or sterol abundance.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
exact_observed_result: Ppp2r1a perturbation induced cholesterol-biosynthesis genes in selected subcortical classes, including Msmo1, Insig1, Dhcr24 and Sc5d in 155 MB Glut and Insig1, Sc5d, Dhcr24 and Msmo1 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. In contrast, the largest thalamic and cortical signatures repressed Srebf2 and Hmgcr at FDR < 0.05.

prior_expectation.summary: Prior work supports the broad molecular function of the perturbed target or complex, while the atlas result refines the affected brain cell type and RNA-output module.

resolved_evidence.description: Upregulation of sterol/cholesterol-associated genes in a subset of Ppp2r1a-responsive neuronal classes.
